elements.name: Google Shape;102;p1

Internal pilot discussion · 13 September 2026
Source: Nayab (2026)

elements.name: Google Shape;199;g9d3d14de9b_0_28
elements.content: DVAM targets the seams where digital value is lost

elements.name: Google Shape;200;g9d3d14de9b_0_28
items: Economics sets value goals. Finance models where value should be created and captured.
IT builds capability. Technology teams optimize what systems can deliver, at what cost and speed.
Management allocates resources. Leaders commit priorities—often before the three views are reconciled.
DVAM closes the gap. It connects the functions in one measurable loop instead of adding another governance layer.

elements.name: Google Shape;167;p2
items: Economic — value creation & capture. Where money enters, moves, and leaves; pricing, revenue, costs, demand, and unit economics.
IT / Technology — value enablement. What systems can deliver, at what cost and speed; infrastructure, data, automation, integration, and skills.
Management — value governance. Who decides, on what evidence, and how fast; strategy, resources, risk, and decision cadence.
Digital Value Core. Economic intent, technical capacity, and management action stay synchronized.

elements.name: Titel 2
elements.content: Three layers converge on one Digital Value Core

elements.name: Google Shape;167;p2
items: 1 · Discovery — Economics ↔ Management. Market and cost signals choose funded bets.
2 · Enablement — IT ↔ Management. Actual technical capacity limits credible commitments.
3 · Realization — IT ↔ Economics. Capability becomes efficiency, revenue, or lower unit cost.
4 · Feedback — all three layers. Actual results recalibrate the next planning cycle.
Closed circuit. Economics → Management → IT → Economics → Feedback.

elements.name: Titel 2
elements.content: Four loops turn alignment into an operating cycle

elements.name: Titel 1
elements.content: TEAI makes alignment measurable on a 0–100 scale

elements.name: Textplatzhalter 2
items: TEAI = (w₁·ITM + w₂·EP + w₃·MA) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + w₃)
ITM · IT Maturity (0–100). Infrastructure reliability, data quality, and automation coverage.
EP · Economic Performance (0–100). Margin trend, cost per transaction, and revenue per digital touchpoint.

elements.name: Textplatzhalter 3
items: MA · Management Agility (0–100). Decision cycle time, cross-functional communication, and resource reallocation speed.
w₁, w₂, w₃ · organization-set weights. Weights reflect which layer matters most or is currently constraining value.
The takeaway. TEAI is a weighted composite: no single strong layer can fully mask weak alignment across the other two.

elements.name: Titel 1
elements.content: Read TEAI as a trend—not a cross-company benchmark

elements.name: Textplatzhalter 2
items: Measure quarterly. Use a short 5–7 question self-assessment for each layer, scored 0–100.
Set weights deliberately. Adjust them as the business matures or the binding constraint changes.
Track the components too. The composite signals alignment; ITM, EP, and MA show where intervention is needed.

elements.name: Textplatzhalter 3
items: Rising TEAI. The three layers are converging.
Flat or falling TEAI. An early warning: technically sound but economically hollow, or economically promising but technically unsupported.
Use directionally. Self-assessment can be biased, weights are subjective, and differently weighted organizations are not directly comparable.

elements.name: Text Placeholder 2
elements.content: A 3-year TEAI trend isn't available from the source paper — DVAM is a conceptual framework, not a longitudinal study. We'd begin building that history with quarterly self-assessments once the pilot starts.

elements.name: Google Shape;167;p2
items: 1 · Map the three layers. Name owners and current connection points.
2 · Establish a baseline TEAI. Score ITM, EP, and MA before changes.
3 · Assign loop owners. Assign accountability for each connection.
4 · Attach TEAI to planning. Review TEAI with budget or sprint decisions.
5 · Iterate the weights. Shift emphasis as constraints move; use TEAI directionally.
